chapter: Chicago boyhood and the Austin High Gang
title: Jazz as the wedding of African rhythm and European harmony
summary: He and Johnston agree jazz is African rhythm joined to European melody and harmony.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And then we recognised it in the jazz. So that is really our first influence and it should be recognised. And as I think you and I talked before we turned the tape on that we both quite agree, I mean to me African rhythms and the rhythms and the sound of the drums and everything like that is your basic jazz beat. To me it's a religion within itself, the beat. It's a feeling that you get inside.
And then with the European harmonies and melodic lines and put that in and make the wedding, make the wedding and now you have American jazz. American music.

American music. The...only one, because every European group brought its own music with it. It's own rhythm. And none of that music became established of course, as you well know, as the American music.
European melody. That's the American music.
That's correct. That's how I've always felt about it too. The melodic line and the harmonies of the Europeans and the African rhythm which is the real.....
Of course that's the Afro-American contribution. the American Constitution.
True, true, true, true. Well that's American jazz.
